description: Last-resort fallback for a real user mistake (cp_loss >= 50) with a clear better_move but NO shape / NO principle / NO firing R-rule. Severity tier respects [[cp-loss-is-not-material]] — never translate cp_loss to 'X pawns lost'. Asymmetric threshold (Mohit 2026-05-21): the bare engine-speak default variant requires cp_loss >= 100, but detector-driven variants (with_blocked_pawn / with_board_state) fire at the lower promotion threshold (50). Rationale: a 50-100cp 'mistake' is a positional preference — calling Bb3 'a mistake' when Bd3 is 14cp better is overharsh and engine-speak. Only label cp_loss 50-100 as a mistake when we have real teaching (detector-driven why-clause). Below 100cp with no detector → silent (the 'silence beats engine-speak' principle).

fact_glossary.severity_phrase: Authored phrase picked from severity_phrases via severity_tiers
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_file: File letter of a user pawn whose advance was blocked by the played piece move. Set by principle_blocked_pawn detector — names an opening principle violation.
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_square: Target square the blocked pawn would have advanced to.
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_would_support: Central pawn square the blocked pawn would have supported diagonally. When set, the with_blocked_pawn_supports variant teaches the specific structural reason; otherwise with_blocked_pawn names the principle generically.
fact_glossary.board_state_clause: Pre-rendered string from board_state_describer (1-3 facts joined). Lower priority than blocked_pawn — when both fire, prefer the named principle.

variants.with_blocked_pawn_supports: {move_san} {severity_phrase} — it blocks your {blocked_pawn_file}-pawn. {best_move} would have supported your {blocked_pawn_would_support} pawn.
variants.with_blocked_pawn: {move_san} {severity_phrase} — it blocks your {blocked_pawn_file}-pawn from advancing to {blocked_pawn_square}. {best_move} was better.
